guide.title: Mozart: Eine kleine Nachtmusik, K. 525 – IV. Rondo (Allegro)
guide.overview: This is a rondo. A rondo is a piece where a main tune keeps coming back between contrasting episodes. Here the tune is in G major and the first violin plays it first. Listen for its returns, and for the way the key and mood change in between. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, and the score came from optical recognition, so small details may be imprecise. The big picture is more reliable.

listening_points.headline: The main tune, soft and light
listening_points.text: The first violin plays the main tune right away [m. 1-3]. It starts softly and climbs up in leaps. The tune is played again at [m. 5-7]. Later in this opening section it gets louder in steps, reaching a strong finish at [m. 10b].

listening_points.headline: Still loud, with the lower strings stepping forward
listening_points.text: The second part begins loud [m. 11]. The cello and viola probably share the lead for a moment [m. 12-13]. Then the instruments move together in the same rhythm [m. 14-15]. The harmony is still in G major.

listening_points.headline: A brighter key, then a sudden hush
listening_points.text: The music moves to D major, a key that sounds fresh and bright [m. 17]. The volume drops to soft at [m. 18]. At times only three instruments play [m. 18, 20-21]. A sharp accent appears at [m. 22].

listening_points.headline: A move to A major, then back
listening_points.text: The key shifts up to A major [m. 25-32]. The first violin leads at first [m. 26]. After that the tune seems shared with the other instruments. The estimated chords here move around a lot. The music then settles back into D major [m. 33].

listening_points.headline: The main tune in D major
listening_points.text: The main tune returns in the first violin, now lower down in D major [m. 37-39]. The lines are more independent here. Each instrument moves a bit on its own.

listening_points.headline: Loud chords: the estimated peak of this section
listening_points.text: The music turns suddenly loud at [m. 48]. All the instruments play chords together, and the peak is probably at [m. 49]. Then it drops back to soft at [m. 51].

listening_points.headline: A turn to C and a darker mood
listening_points.text: The key moves to C major [m. 57a-58b]. The cello then plays the main tune low down [m. 58b-61]. A new part begins loud [m. 59], with the instruments playing the same notes in unison. The mood turns darker in C minor and gets soft at [m. 60].

listening_points.headline: Warm E-flat major, then louder
listening_points.text: The key brightens to E-flat major [m. 62]. The first violin plays the main tune again [m. 64-66]. The music gets louder at [m. 68] and stays loud to the end of this stretch.

listening_points.headline: Stormy G minor, loud and urgent
listening_points.text: The key turns to G minor, which sounds more serious [m. 72-75]. The software marks a brief turn away from G minor at [m. 76-77], but its chord estimates there are unclear. Then the minor key returns [m. 78-85]. The first violin leads clearly, and the volume stays loud.

listening_points.headline: Hushed passage, leading toward home
listening_points.text: The music drops to soft again [m. 86]. Three instruments play lightly in D major and then G major [m. 86-89]. Then the harmony returns to D major [m. 92-100]. It sets up the return of the main tune.

listening_points.headline: The main tune comes home
listening_points.text: The main tune returns in G major, played softly by the first violin [m. 101-103]. It repeats at [m. 105-107], this time an octave lower than before.

listening_points.headline: The lead passes around
listening_points.text: The lead probably moves around here. It may go to the cello [m. 110-112], then the second violin [m. 113-115]. These guesses are uncertain, so think of it as shared. Then the music gets loud at [m. 116].

listening_points.headline: A detour through F and C
listening_points.text: The music wanders to F major [m. 124-128], where a sudden accent falls at [m. 125]. Then it moves to C major [m. 129-132]. Listen for the loud unison at [m. 132], where the last part begins.

listening_points.headline: Final return of the main tune
listening_points.text: Right after that unison, the main tune returns in G major, played softly by the first violin [m. 133-135]. It comes back again at [m. 137-139]. The first violin leads most of this stretch, which stays soft until [m. 149].

listening_points.headline: Loud, bright finish in G major
listening_points.text: The music gets loud at [m. 149]. A brief visit to D major follows, with the second violin probably leading [m. 150-154]. Then G major returns for good at [m. 155]. The last measures are loud and the instruments play chords together, ending in G major.

glossary.explanation: A piece where a main tune returns again and again, with different music in between.
The home note and scale that a passage is built around. Major keys sound bright, and minor keys sound darker.
A change from one key to another.
All the instruments play the same notes, or the same notes in different octaves.
The instruments move together in the same rhythm, like a hymn.
Only three of the four instruments are playing; one is resting.
p means soft. f means loud. mf is medium loud. sf and fp mark a sudden accent or a loud note followed by soft.
